title: $10M CEO: How to Get Ahead while Others Get Replaced | Daniel Priestley
guestTitle: Entrepreneur, Author, and Founder of multiple multi-million dollar businesses
aboutGuest: Daniel Priestley is a serial entrepreneur and author who was named UK Entrepreneur of the Year, having built and scaled multiple businesses that collectively generate over $10 million in revenue. In recent years, he has successfully transformed several of his ventures into AI-driven companies. He is also the author of an entrepreneurship book for kids and a sought-after speaker on the future of work and business in the AI age.
summary: Marina Mogilko interviews Daniel Priestley, UK Entrepreneur of the Year, about how AI will reshape the economy and eliminate repetitive jobs over the next five years. Priestley argues that entrepreneurial skills — such as pitching, ideation, rapid testing, and community building — are the critical moats in the new AI-driven economy. He also shares how he built a $100K/month business using GPT wrappers and explains why APIs and AI automation tools represent a massive opportunity for entrepreneurs right now.
keyTakeaways: AI will likely decimate wages within 5 years by automating repetitive, functional jobs — making entrepreneurial adaptability the most important skill to develop now.

Classical economics defines 4 moats — land, labor, capital, and enterprise — and we are shifting into the 'enterprise' era, where spotting opportunities and commercializing them quickly is the dominant advantage.
The 4 must-learn skills for the AI era are: crafting experiences, building communities and personal brands, fostering high-velocity team culture, and aligning teams around innovation.
Priestley built a $100K/month business by leveraging GPT wrappers, demonstrating that APIs and AI tools offer a golden opportunity for entrepreneurs who act early.
The schooling system is rooted in the industrial age and fails to prepare people for today's economy — individuals must proactively upskill and embrace plural, entrepreneurial careers.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Priestley
transcript.text: No, it's not a bad way to park money, but being a land owner was a very big moat in the agricultural age. Then the next moat was labor and capital. So we call the four moats land, labor, capital, enterprise. So the fourth moat that we're moving into is the enterprise moat. So enterprise moat means that you know how to spot opportunities, assemble teams and commercialize opportunities at speed. So there are essentially people who are comfortable and know how to go through that cycle really quickly. And essentially the skills that are the most relevant skills right now are these kind of soft skills, these entrepreneurial skills, things like pitching, things like visioning, things like ideation, rapid testing, conducting fast cheap experiments to figure out what works, understanding multiple disciplines so that you can understand context and then bring stuff together.
